learningGoals: Understand and sequence the events of a simple story about problem-solving. 🧠
Identify and pronounce new words related to birds and nature. 🌳
Comprehend the moral of the story: thinking smartly helps solve problems. 💡
Practice reading aloud with expression, especially when the crow is thirsty and happy. 🗣️
Recognize the difference between 'some', 'little', and 'more' in the context of water. 💧
conversationStarters: What do you do when you feel very thirsty after playing outside? 🏃‍♂️
Have you ever seen a crow near your house? What sound does it make? 🎶
If you were the crow, how would you have reached the water? 🤔
teachingTips: Use a clear glass and some pebbles to demonstrate how dropping stones makes the water level rise. 🪨
Encourage your child to narrate the story in their own words using picture cues. 🖼️
Emphasize the 'c' sound in words like 'crow' and 'clever'. 🗣️
Discuss why the crow didn't give up and why trying hard is important. 💪
Ask your child to draw the story to check their understanding of the beginning, middle, and end. 🖍️

funActivities.title: Water and Pebbles Experiment 🧪
funActivities.description: Fill a clear cup halfway with water. Let your child drop small stones or marbles into the cup one by one and watch the water rise, just like the crow did!

funActivities.title: Act Like a Crow 🎭
funActivities.description: Play a role-play game where your child acts out flying, looking for water, feeling thirsty, and dropping stones while you read the story aloud.

funActivities.title: Story Sequencing Cards 🃏
funActivities.description: Draw 3-4 scenes from the story on small pieces of paper. Mix them up and ask your child to arrange them in the correct order.
